content: Hi Drew, I'm preparing a training packet outline for a 32-person cohort (modules: account setup, data handling, incident reporting; planned format: PDF; date July 8). Since it must be usable by the entire cohort, what accessibility requirements should I build in (e.g., tagged PDF, alt text, screen-reader-friendly structure, alternative formats)? Any guidance is appreciated.
I do not hold additional task-specific information.

Hi Morgan, I'm preparing a training packet outline for a 32-person cohort (modules: account setup, data handling, incident reporting; PDF; July 8). It needs to be usable by the entire cohort, including people with disabilities. What accessibility features should the PDF include (tagged structure, alt text for images, reading order, color contrast, plain-language summaries, alternative formats)? Any other must-haves?
The accessibility coordinator knows that several participants use screen readers and recommends tagged headings, descriptive links, and alt text for diagrams.

{"baseline_summary": {"date": "July 8", "modules": ["account setup", "data handling", "incident reporting"], "format": "PDF", "cohort_size": 32}, "recommendation": "Build the training packet as a single accessible PDF with one section per module, in this order: account setup, data handling, incident reporting. Start with a short overview page listing the three modules, the July 8 date, and how to request an alternative format. Use real document structure: tagged PDF, logical heading levels (H1 for the packet, H2 for each module, H3 for subsections), a reading order that matches the visual order, and descriptive link text (not 'click here'). Provide alt text for every diagram or screenshot and do not rely on color alone to convey meaning. Keep text legible with good contrast. Because several cohort members use screen readers, test the final PDF with a screen reader before distribution. Also offer the packet in at least one alternative format (for example, an accessible Word or plain-text version) on request, so the full cohort of 32 can use it.
